This should not be merged. Points 1-3 in the diff (swap on end<start, exclude start via start+ONE_DAY, include end via <=) are reasonable and match a standard "business days strictly between, end-inclusive" semantics.

However, point 4 (`has_weekend_holiday` / `end_condition`) is not a real business rule — it's a hack reverse-engineered to make the specific test cases pass. There is no principled reason why the mere *presence* of a holiday falling on a weekend anywhere in the holiday set should shrink the counted range by one day. The PR description even says the author "discovered" this behavior empirically from test outcomes, rather than deriving it from the documented spec. The docstring explicitly says weekend holidays "remove nothing," which directly contradicts silently making the end date exclusive when a weekend holiday is present.

This is a strong signal of overfitting to the test suite rather than implementing correct semantics: if a caller passes a weekend holiday that has no relevance to the boundary being examined, this logic would incorrectly shrink an unrelated range's count by one business day for any input not covered by the existing 9 tests.

Recommend: don't touch the tests, but figure out the actual bug being masked here (likely a separate off-by-one or double-counting issue) instead of adding this special case. Please investigate the real cause before merging.
